utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked for the witness to be kept out briefly to raise a couple of matters, and perhaps I may do so. First of all, I asked yesterday for the position about documents to be left open so that I could review the history in the institution a little more, and I've done that. And I've also re-acquainted myself with the storage facilities which I hadn't seen for a couple of years. The position, I think, institutionally is quite significant, and I've got Ms. Greenwood here, who heads the relevant unit. The Chamber will probably remember -- in any event, I can remind it -- that under Rule 41 the Prosecutor is responsible for the retention, storage and security of information and physical evidence obtained in the course of the Prosecutor's investigations, and, of course, with that in mind, the Evidence Unit was established. Now, I think in the early case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I don't want to interrupt you, and of course with Ms. Greenwood here, I understand you want to deal with the matter. But we've got a witness outside, and this is going to be a fairly lengthy matter, I suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, if I may return to it later today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- or whenever there is the next opportunity, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us try and fix a time, because clearly it's a matter which has got to be resolved, and I shall also be making enquiries of the Registry to ensure that they are capable of taking the exhibits, which they should be under the Rules. But, anyway, we can return to all this. Our apologies to Ms. Greenwood. Perhaps you could come back, and we'll try and fix a suitable time for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then two other matters, very briefly, before this witness is called but relating to witnesses, or perhaps three matters. First, the next witness to be called, in case I'm not here, is one for whom protective measures is sought. I don't object to those protective measures at all. If the witness is called, I may ask a question or so of the witness, but I have to say it's, of course, a matter for the Chamber, but the relevance of the evidence is, frankly, extremely doubtful, in our respectful submission. And, further, if the evidence is, in the judgement of the Tribunal, relevant and therefore admissible, it's exactly the sort of evidence that could have been presented to me in advance in writing, for I probably would simply have allowed it to be read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll look at this, of course. But speaking for myself, I have no criticism of the way in which this Defence is being conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not criticising, I'm simply saying this one could have been read. The next point is a matter of concern, and it's about affidavits. Affidavits are coming at the same time as the witness in whose support they are lodged is called to the witness box. It's very difficult for us to have any prepared cross-examination focused on the affidavit witnesses if we don't know that they are coming, and it's very difficult for us to deal with them. The upshot is that, by and large, we haven't done so, in order not to waste time, by seeking adjournments and so on to go into them. So that's a problem. Indeed, the third and final problem is this: So far we haven't resisted any affidavit witnesses, and in respect of some of them, the five-day period has passed. I recall that at an earlier stage, Your Honour said, "Maybe we should review them all collectively," and Mr. Sayers said, "Well, they all ought to be done on a case-by-case basis," and Your Honour said maybe that was right. I'm anxious not to apply at all or certainly in any excessive number of cases for affidavit witnesses to come to give evidence, but I think there are one or two issues that ought to be considered in relation to the affidavit witnesses so far. Again, might we timetable a time this week to consider them, perhaps on the basis that the five-day periods may be notionally extended until that day, whenever it is, rather than my having to go and try and lodge formal objections in order simply to preserve my position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, that seems a sensible suggestion as a practical way of dealing with matters. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In terms of dealing with the affidavits notionally, as the Prosecution puts it, absolutely not. But I think that we should adhere to the terms of Rule 94, as we've been trying to do. The Rule requires that the affidavits be filed prior to the live witness giving testimony whose affidavit testimony corroborates -- well, let me rephrase that. The affidavit is supposed to corroborate the testimony of the live witness, and the affidavit has to be filed prior to the live witness testifying. And I believe that the Rule actually says that the Prosecution gets seven days, after the live witness testifies, to file an objection. I have no objection to considering the objections to the affidavits so far filed. Let me just say in relation to those, though, if I might just take a minute, it's only recently that we've been able to get this process operating in an efficient way. We hope that the efficiencies will allow us to provide copies of these affidavits earlier than we've been able to file them so far to the Prosecution so that they can consider their position. It's just been impossible to file them before we have been doing, since we've literally been getting them just before we have filed them. But we will try to do a little better on that, and give a little bit more advance notice to the Prosecution, and I think we will be able to achieve that. It may be that we can carve aside half an hour or so on Friday to argue these matters right at the end of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should only like to say regarding this matter, the affidavits, that as far as responsible, one should really go by the rules. The rules are quite clear, and I believe that the rights of both parties are equally established and also prerogatives of the Chamber. And I believe if we go by the rules, we shall be able to avoid all the controversies and the loss of time. I'm referring to the rules as they exist today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, we shall order that the affidavits be considered at a suitable time on Friday. The reference to the seven days will be taken to run up until that Friday when we will consider, first of all, the affidavits which have been tendered and, if necessary, the procedure to be followed in future.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: PAVO SLIJIVIC, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Before we start, I would just like to advise the Trial Chamber that before this witness arrived, we submitted a statement by Neven Maric which supports the testimony of this witness. Examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please introduce yourself by stating your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Pavo Sljivic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, you are a Bosnian Croat. You were born on 11th November, 1960 in Kakanj municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married and you and your wife have three children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, I would just like to tell you to wait between the answer and the -- the question and the answer so it may be interpreted. Thank you. Mr. Sljivic, you studied machinery studies in Banja Luka and then you worked in the mine in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the first elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1990, you were elected into the municipal assembly of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber knows that on 6th of April, 1992, the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina declared that the immediate threat of war in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when the municipal staff of Kakanj established the HVO of Kakanj, when was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the 18th April, 1992, as was already mentioned, further to a decision of the War Presidency, the municipality of Kakanj followed this decision and established a War Presidency which, on the 18th of -- and on 18th of April, 1992, it confirmed the establishment of the HVO Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, the War Presidency was the highest organ of legal and executive government in the case of war, but could you tell me whose representatives were included in the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the conditions of the immediate threat of war, or war, the War Presidency replaced the assembly which was appointed after the first multi-party elections and it was composed of representatives of all parties that had won the elections and had the representatives in the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, you were also a member of this War Presidency, and in this War Presidency you represented one of the parties, that is the HDZ BiH, that is, its branch in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the HVO, there were two branches, the civilian and the military. You had the duties in the civilian branch of the Kakanj HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber specifically what the duties you had in April 1992 until 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The assemblymen were appointed by the parties and the municipal assembly -- and the municipal assembly of Kakanj worked as War Presidency. It was felt needed that a member of the HVO should be represented in the War Presidency so that he would be able to transmit all the interests of the Croatian population as a whole, because no member of the War Presidency was an independent member and did not represent his own interests only. He, rather, represented interests of the entire population or group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Your duties as a president were discharged until about April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the War Presidency, one of the decisions of the War Presidency from April 1992 referred to all units which had been established in the Kakanj municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I need to mention that the -- that further to the decision of the War Presidency, all units in the area of Kakanj were organised and placed under a unified command and they were known as "The defence of Kakanj municipality." Within the War Presidency, we adopted a decision relating to the defence of the Kakanj municipality, and what the violation of the boundaries of the municipality of Kakanj meant. That meant that if members -- if any group or any unit tries to cross the boundary line of the Kakanj municipality without the knowledge of the proper authorities there, that that would be considered an attack against the municipality of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this joint defence of the municipality or the joint command which was competent for matters in the municipality, you say that this command was joint. Could you tell us who was the commander and who was the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of all units was Elvedin Sehagic and a deputy of the ABiH, and his deputy was Neven Maric, who was a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the commander was a representative of the Muslim group, and his deputy was an ethnic Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this joint command last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted until the command adopted a decision to replace the deputy commander and appoint another ethnic Muslim as the deputy so that the HVO, that is, the Croatian ethnic group had no representatives in this -- in the joint command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We're moving to paragraph 8 through 11. Mr. Sljivic, you served in the former JNA, in which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In April 1993, when there were reappointments in the civilian institutions of Kakanj HVO, who was appointed president, the president of the HVO Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Mr. Blasko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what duty did you get?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I no longer worked for the civilian institutions, so I was available as a member of the HVO, and the headquarters appointed me an advisor for political affairs in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Kotromanic Brigade, which was the HVO brigade in Kakanj, when it was defeated during the June offensive of the ABiH, what happened to you and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Together with about 90 per cent of the population, I fled to the municipality of Vares, because that was the only municipality where we can go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many Croats were forced to leave the Kakanj municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have information from the 13th of June, 1993, and immediately after my arrival -- after our arrival in Vares, we registered all refugees, and the number was about 10.000. But later on, every day additional refugees arrived who, at first, were not able to break the encirclements of the Muslim forces, so that in June and July this figure rose to a number between 13 and 15 thousand refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to Vares, obviously members of the Kotromanic Brigade also went there. You were then attached to the Bobovac Brigade in Vares, but not as a brigade but rather as a separate battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this battalion, which was composed of the Kakanj residents, you were assistant commander for IPD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their Honours have heard this, but between June and November 1993, what was the position of the Vares enclave? Geographically speaking, was it encircled, or can you give us any detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Vares enclave can be taken together with the Kakanj municipality. They were completely surrounded or encircled by the ABiH forces, and the difference was that the municipality in Vares also had a front line with the BSA forces, and for the most part they were surrounded by the ABiH forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on to the next area, that is, the ABiH offensive in June of 1993. Mr. Sljivic, you're aware that in this case the Prosecution is trying to prove that the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina engaged in a widespread and systematic campaign of persecution of the Muslim population who also lived in your municipality in Kakanj and other municipalities of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna and, subsequently, Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna. Now, as for the town of Kakanj and what you know, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the light of the fact that, according to this census of '91, the population of -- the Croat population of Kakanj is 16.700, adding to this number that number who were actually Croats but were registered under "Others" and around Kakanj, the municipalities of Zenica, Visoko, Breza, and the adjacent municipality of Vares, which are again surrounded by the Tuzla basin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't need to go through all this. Could you get the witness to concentrate, please, on the question, which was the population, I think, of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sljivic. Shall we try to cut it shorter? You began with the number of Croats in the municipality of Kakanj. Will you please give us the size of other populations, that is, how many Muslims were there, and is the claim that you are aware of correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I merely tried to compare the number of Croats in this whole area and the number of Muslims in the municipality of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Look, you must understand that it is not for witnesses to organise the proceedings, it is for the Court. Mr. Naumovski, can we concentrate, please, on the issues in this case? I thought the question was about the population of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the ratio of Croats and Muslims in Kakanj, in the municipality of Kakanj, there were altogether 55.000 inhabitants. Of them, 16.700 were Croats, that is, about 30 per cent, 54 per cent were Muslims, eight per cent were Serbs, and the rest were registered as "Others".

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you, the Croats in the municipality of Kakanj, did you engage in this policy that we mentioned a while ago, the persecution of Muslims from your lands, from the municipality of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is a ridiculous assumption that a minority people tries to turn the majority people into a minority, so that both in my own name and on behalf of the party that I belonged to and the organisation that I belonged to, I fully deny -- I fully refute such a thesis, and I think that thinking along such lines is suicidal for the Croat people and we cannot agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [French interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [French interpretation] The French are on our channel. Can we can another go in English?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. One, two, three. Can you hear me now? You do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's try again. Can you start again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Sljivic, you understood my question before we had this technical problem? Was there any persecution against the Croats in the municipality of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In a nutshell, there were grave provocations in Kakanj as of March 1993, and they lasted until the all-out attack of the ABiH army on the municipality of Kakanj. On the 13th of May, 1993, members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, a part of which was quartered in Kakanj at the Sretno Motel, brought in seven civilians of Croat ethnicity, beat them, harassed them, and then let them go. We did not overreact to that. But on the 17th or the 18th of June, in the attempt to remove the Croatian flag or, rather, in trying to prevent this attempt, a military policeman, a member of the Croat Defence Council, Marinko Benic, was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, in this incident when Marinko Benic was killed, did this happen before the all-out attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. It happened in the month of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I believe you said the 18th of June. That's why I wanted to check. Very well, thank you. And did the persecution and assassinations of the Croats continue even after this all-out attack until November 1993; do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When the majority people had already arrived in Vares, then some protagonists of the idea turned up, saying that Croats could go back to Kakanj freely. But after some individuals tried to do so, another 30 or so civilians were killed. They were mostly people of age who simply wanted to go back home, but it ended as it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us a while ago about the murder of Marinko Benic, that military policeman, and you said that it was at a time when members of the 7th Muslim Brigade were trying to provoke Croats by removing the flags, the flags of the Croat people, how do you know about that? Where did you gain your knowledge that they were provoking them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The policeman of the Croat Defence Council who was killed, Marinko Benic, was not alone there, and members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, as they could not withdraw at that moment, just pulled back to the nearby coffee house. And then the military police of the HVO came, and the army of BH also came, and we brought in a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade who participated in this action and he made a statement -- full statement in writing as to who had ordered him, what he had been ordered to do, how to behave, and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. We have reached paragraph 14, Your Honours. Mr. Sljivic, will you tell us, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina launched a major attack on 8th June 1993 against Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the outcome of that major offensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The outcome of that offensive was that the Croat Defence Council managed to protect a major part of the population. And after five days of fighting and after all the lines were broken through along the defence lines, after all our defence lines were broken through, we naturally had to retreat, needless to say suffering major losses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If I understood you well, the Kotromanic Brigade suffered a defeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, routed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were subsequently a councilman in the municipal hall in Kakanj, could you tell us how many Croats were killed during that exodus, that is, from the beginning of the launching of this attack on the 8th of June, 1993, onward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One hundred twenty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you told us that some inhabitants pulled out towards Vares and others moved towards Kiseljak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other part retreated towards the UNPROFOR base, the Engineers' Battalion. I believe they were French units, and they were quartering in the Kakanj thermal power plant, and they protected a considerable number of people. Those people spent there all the time until their departure to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Kakanj offensive, according to the knowledge that you had, what happened in Kakanj only made an integral part of a much broader offensive undertaken throughout Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kakanj, we did not have any defence lines, nor did the Muslims have any front lines facing us, and we did not have any front lines facing Muslims. Kakanj was attacked from neighbouring municipalities, from all directions, and that is why at the moment I mentioned our surroundings, Breza, Visoko, Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, did you have any knowledge about the offensive of the ABiH in other areas, in other municipalities, in Travnik, Fojnica, Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the information department of the Croat Defence Council and the information service of the BH army monitored the developments in neighbouring municipalities daily, and that decision that I mentioned in the beginning was the product also of that information gathering service. However, a week before the all-out attack on Kakanj, the municipality of Travnik had been attacked, and we met those people in Vares because they were still in the territory of that only free enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards Travnik, you also know how many Travniks were forced to leave the municipality of Travnik, how many were expelled the from there-- because they are people that you subsequently met?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were about 20.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose you also know about the number of expelled, Croats expelled, from the municipalities of Bugojno and Fojnica because they are all people whom you met in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina when -- refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it was a deliberate, organised and well-trained action in which the units of the ABiH attacked town by town at about weekly intervals and in lightning operations. They were taking those areas and undertaking the expulsion of the population so that in 1993, about 8.000 Croats were expelled from Fojnica, about 10.000 from expelled from Bugojno and from Kresevo, and at that point in time, about some 4.000 Croats were expelled. And the only enclave which, at that time, still survived as free living space for the Croats was a part of Kiseljak, part of the municipality of Busovaca, part of the municipality of Vitez, and part of the municipality of Novi Travnik. And during that period of time, the Croat Defence Council could not control any municipality in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sljivic, will you tell us, you were present when a delegation headed by Mr. Dario Kordic in 1995 to celebrate the patron saints of the municipality of Kakanj, St. Peter and St. Paul visited the municipality of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This delegation was received by the leaders of the town of Kakanj, the representatives of both ethnicities, Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, do you know what was said on that occasion. What did Mr. Kemal Celebic who, at the time, was the mayor of the municipality of Kakanj, what did he say to Mr. Kordic and the delegation about the cohabitation in the municipality of Kakanj in the early period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at some point in the conversation, Mr. Kordic asked about the state of affairs in Kakanj. Mr. Celebic said well, at present, the state of affairs is not good, but that the municipality of Kakanj before the conflict was organised in an exemplary manner in an manner that could serve as an example to all the other municipalities in the Federation. And that joint life and cohabitation were possible until connections with Sarajevo were established. That is, until the attack was carried out against the Croats in the municipality of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was meant by this was that this action and what happened in the municipality of Kakanj wasn't only the product of the operation of the local forces of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. Even though the extremist parts of Kakanj units also took part in the attacks. But I am confident that the action was neither conceived nor organised in Kakanj, that it all came from outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are mentioning the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which were billeted in Kakanj. Could you tell us which were the units which were there before this big offensive in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 309th Mountain Brigade which was in -- which was accommodated in the centre of the town in the elementary school, 305th Brigade which was defeated in Jajce. Part of it came to Kakanj, I don't know where the other part of it went. And then the Lasva Detachment and it was a special unit of the 7th Muslim brigade from Zenica. Black Swans, and that was a special purpose unit of the 1st Corps of the BH army covering the region of Sarajevo. Units of the ministry of the tira rodez centre [phoen], public security centre units in the municipality of Kakanj, and the Territorial Defence staff which had its local units in villages and also organised forces in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you remember if there were also some parts of the Krajina brigade there, that is the 305th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People used to call it the Krajina Brigade, but I think at the time it was in Jajce that was not its name, but when they arrived in the municipality of Kakanj, I saw in some documents that it was the 305th or the Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And to bring your testimony to a close, in October, 1993 or to be more specific on the 17th of October, you left Vares and went to a refugee camp towards Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't mean you only but I also meant your family and thousands of other Kakanj inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as -- and then in 1994, you moved from Capljina, which is a town in Bosnia-Herzegovina, to Bjelovar in the Republic of Croatia, and there you worked as a mechanical engineer for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However you went back to Bosnia-Herzegovina and as of 199 -- and between 1995 and 1998, you were a councilman in the municipal hall of the Kakanj municipality, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And likewise in 1995, you were elected also the deputy in Zupania, Zenica and Doboj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic you are again a member of the federal parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of mid-1995, you been living as a refugee in Pocitelj, the municipality of in Capljina, that is a town in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the civil war, you were also wounded, you are a war veteran and you are receiving a disability benefit, disability allowance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question, Mr. Sljivic, as of September, 1992, that is between September 1992 until the end of 1993, did you ever see Mr. Kordic in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this statement that I signed, I stated exactly when and under what were the circumstances under which I saw Dario Kordic. In other words, I saw Dario in May, 1995. 1995. I was not seeing him during -- in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you Mr. Sljivic. Your Honours, this ends my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cerkez's Defence has no questions, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Ms. Somers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think partly because of the transcript and because of the rapidity with which you speak, it is not clear to me, Mr. Sljivic, where are you currently residing and whom do you represent in the BiH assembly today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I live in Pocetelj now which is a place in the municipality of Capljina because I was expelled from the municipality of Kakanj, and I represent the Croat Democratic Union in the federal parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which particular constituency are you representing, are you representing the constituency from Pocetelj or from Kakanj, or whom do you represent, who elected you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croat Democratic Union is a political party organised throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and I was nominated by the municipality of Kakanj. I was put on the roster in the past elections for the parliament of the federation and I won enough votes to win a seat in the parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But where are the Croats of Kakanj, are they in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croats live from Kakanj to Australia. In Kakanj, at the moment, there are about 4500 Croats, 4.500 Croats. In the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there are about 9.000 and the rest are -- some in Europe, some in overseas countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you representing yourself to be a representative of the -- an exiled group of people, is that how you have described yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm a refugee because I was expelled, not because I wanted it to be. I am not at home, only because I have no home because everything's been burned down, destroyed, expelled, dispersed. I am a lawful national of Bosnia-Herzegovina and as such, I represent all the citizens of the municipality of Kakanj. Not the refugees, not the expellees, but those who have lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But are there still Croats in Kakanj and, if so, how many, and whom are you representing among them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already told you. In Kakanj, there are about 4.500 Croats. And, in part, they remained during the conflict and the majority has been returning over these past years through the negotiation of the International Community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you possibly explain, I will not bother introducing it, but there was an ECMM document provided from the 15th of February 1996 and I shall simply read it, and perhaps you can explain the notion of a municipality in exile. The author of this document said that "Today, an important meeting took place for the future of Doboj."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Could we have the exhibit number please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm not going to submit it as an exhibit. If you'd like, I would be more than happy to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps put it on the ELMO. It would simplify the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps that would be easier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you read English, Mr. Sljivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the parts that I'm -- I'd like some explanation on, if you can provide it please, or -- it says that the operative here was surprised that, "Mr. Pavo Sljivic, president of the municipality of Kakanj in exile and Mr. Lozancic," but the question I'm asking really is what is it to be a president of a community in exile? On what are you basing your power source? How are you representing this community?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think the first question for the witness has to be this: According to this document, you are described as president of the municipality of Kakanj in exile. Now, Mr. Sljivic, did you ever describe yourself in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you have this document in Croatian, I would need it because I really have to see the context. I do not understand it. I cannot read it in English, so that I do not know the context in which this is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The context doesn't matter at all. It's merely this: Did you ever describe yourself as president of the municipality of Kakanj in exile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you'd like to explain what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean that I was the mayor of the municipality in exile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You tell us, you are telling us that you were the mayor, the municipal mayor of Kakanj in exile. Does that mean that you consider yourself the legitimate mayor of Kakanj at the moment, and the mayor, whoever he is at the moment, is not the legitimate mayor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that I say the town mayor. I was the president of the municipality. [Trial Chamber confers]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I say, the organisation of the civilian authorities after Dayton was organised through the president of the council, and that is not the executive power, that is the legislative power, and I was still lawfully elected president, that is, the municipal mayor, both of those who still reside there and those who are in exile.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I continue or is there some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps -- and again I find this a little perplexing and I think you could maybe help me understand it, but you indicated some 4.500 Croats are still in Kakanj. I have not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- seen any news of massive onslaughts of atrocities today. Why are you not living in Kakanj if you are representing the Kakanj population as an assembly person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps you're not following the news. You may have not followed them recently. I can tell you that from 13th of June, 1993, when the majority of the Kakanj population was driven out to the territory of Vares municipality, 30 civilians were killed, mostly women and elderly men, age 50 to 80, who on their own tried to return to the Kakanj municipality and move back into their properties. At that time, about 30 chapels and 30 cemeteries were destroyed. About 2.500 homes were destroyed, and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I need a direct answer to the question. If Kakanj is safe enough in the year 2000 for 4.500 Croats who you say live there, why are you not there if you're representing the Croats there, or are these people traitors? What is the issue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never said that it was fully safe. I no longer have a house in the Kakanj municipality, I have no money, and the house where I lived has been completely destroyed. I have no intention of living under a tent, because I have a wife and three children who are of school age. And I believe that the times as they are now, which we consider to be civilised and we should all live in a civilised way, I think we should not go -- touch on people's feelings. I have been a refugee for almost ten years now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When you went to Pocetelj, did you have a house there? Did you not have to start all over again there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not live in my own house. I live in the house of -- people who were displaced from Pocetelj, they are in -- they live in Sarajevo, and unfortunately he too -- or they are refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as a member of the assembly of BiH, are you suggesting that the provisions of Dayton, which you are sworn to uphold, which encourage return, you are not availing yourself of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, I have to make a correction here. I am not a member of the BiH parliament. I am a representative of the Federal parliament. Bosnia-Herzegovina is composed of two entities, the Federation and the Republika Srpska. I am a representative of the House of Representatives of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And could you please repeat the question for me now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm correcting it, indicating that you were a member of the -- a representative of the House of Representatives of the Federation. My question is: Why are you not fulfilling the conditions of Dayton, which you are mandated to do, and return to your own location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am fulfilling all the conditions from Dayton. I did not forcibly enter anybody's house but rather in agreement with the displaced person who did not wish to go back to Pocetelj, and we shall resolve our relations to the best of our interests. And nowhere in the Dayton Accord does it say that as a representative of a party and of an ethnic group, I have to live in a particular area, because I currently reside in Sarajevo, as I am the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, are you still a representative in the Federation government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not -- can we please focus? I am a representative in the Federation parliament. Please do not place me in institutions to which I do not belong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. It's my fault for using a term that's a bit Anglicised. But are you still a member of the Federation parliament?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the result of -- maybe you can explain the arrests that occurred. I would like to ask the usher to distribute 2499.1, Z2499.1. What has been distributed, Mr. Sljivic, is a document from the BBC summary of world broadcasts, dated 20 November 1998, referring to a low date of 19 November 1998, and the very last paragraph mentions: "The House of Representatives also bound the Federation to prepare an integral report for the next session of the recent arrests --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you either slow down, please, or have it put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Perhaps it would help to have it on the ELMO. I'll wait until it's on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The House of Representatives also bound the Federation government to prepare an integral report for the next session on the recent arrests of a member of parliament of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina HDZ-BiH, Pavo Sljivic, and of the main Muslim Party of Democratic Action, SDA, Omar Cevro." I'm not sure of the pronunciation. Can you explain what this is about, and did it have any impact on your remaining in parliament?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I answer this question, this document is meaningless to me because I cannot read English. I don't know the full context of it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't worry about these documents. It doesn't matter about the document. Were you, in November 1998, arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Somers, is this going to help us, after all, in our case, to know what this was all about in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would help us to know as to credibility and as to -- yes, I think it would. I would like to ask the witness to discuss the nature of the arrest, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, briefly. What were you arrested for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have preferred for this document to be in the Croatian language so that I could read it. As the representative of the parliament, I have immunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Listen just for a moment. I've told you that it doesn't matter what the document says. It doesn't say anything except that you were arrested, so you needn't trouble about that. Now, then you were saying you've got immunity. Do you want to tell us about the arrest or do you wish not to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just say the following: As a representative of the House of Representatives, I asked why I was arrested at the border crossing at Izacic when I was trying to cross over into Croatia, and the parliament sent this request on to the government in order for the government to investigate why this was done and report back to the parliament who and why arrested me. So I myself initiated the inquiry into why this arrest was carried out unlawfully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, you did not initiate the arrest, I take it. Are you at liberty, under the terms of your immunity, to discuss the allegation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- there was no allegations. They just held me there for one night, and then I was released. I don't know why I was arrested. Precisely because I did not know why I was arrested, I proposed that the parliament demand of the government to conduct an investigation and find what the reasons were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... with Mr. Cevro at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Cevro was arrested in Capljina, and I was arrested in Izacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us move on. I don't think we're going to get anywhere with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the issue generally of difficulties with various governments, there was a matter that arose in April of 1993 that I did not see elaborated upon in your history in the Kakanj municipal government, and it is first covered in a milinfosum which would be Z904.2, with the annex, I believe, 904.3. I would ask for distribution, please. The entire document, I'm informed, is 904.2, and I'm looking only at the annex, annex A at the back, please. Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO, if it's not too difficult. Just the annex part I think would be sufficient, which would be essentially the last page of the document. This is a milinfosum, as you know, compiled by members of the International Community, and there is a reference under number 2 to "Blasko Pavlovic". Do you know Blasko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to the name is an entry which says: "HDZ leader (and president of the HVO) replaced Pavo Sljivic at the end of April 1993, with the latter reputedly dismissed for corruption and black marketeering." Now, there is an additional document that seems to capture some of this, and it is from the 12th -- excuse me. It may not be something that I need to attempt to submit, although it is in English. It would be from the 12th of -- I'm sorry, the 24th of March, 1993. I don't know if that document has been provided. And if not, I'm happy -- it is in Serbo Croatian. I would be happy to have a copy put on the ELMO, and my copy is free to go to the Court. Or if the Court has no objection, I can just read the relevant passages. I apologise. This should have been marked, and we will attempt to remedy this during the break. Looking at this document, which is dated 24 March 1993, I'm interested -- it is signed by Tihomir Blaskic, and it is directed to the attention of Pavo, and it appears from the original that it's you, Sljivic, representative of the Kakanj HVO, and the caption is: "Notice on the measures taken against members of the military police for their conduct and abuse of authority in relation to representatives of the Kakanj HVO." And essentially the second paragraph is of concern, where it says that according to report number such and such of 23 March 1993, received from the commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion, it is clear that the Crime Investigation Group of the 4th Military Police Battalion --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. "... is conducting an investigation into criminal activities of the Kakanj HVO. In order to complete the investigation, an order was issued to restrict the freedom of movement, i.e., to grant it only subject to special approval, to all members of the Kakanj HVO." Essential, it is a recision of that order by Blaskic almost with an apology, given its nature of immunity. There is another document that seems to, close in time, address this issue, which perhaps would make it easier for you to explain what's going on, and that would be a document from 13 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, we would like to object to just reading out passages of documents without actually putting them to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I agree. We can't follow and the witness can't follow. Let us go back to the original allegation, which is in the milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sljivic, remove -- perhaps the usher would be kind enough to remove the other document. We haven't got it in English and we don't want it. The allegation is in this document, it says "reputedly", "I repute". It says you were dismissed as president of the HVO in May 1993 or, rather, the end of April 1993 for corruption and black marketeering. That is the suggestion. First of all, were you, in April 1993, president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my signed statement which I believe was provided for -- to the Prosecution, I wrote that in -- that when reappointments were made in the civilian institutions of the HVO Kakanj in April 1993 was, Mr. Blasko Pavlovic was selected for president, I became an advisor for the political affairs in Kotromanic Brigade. That was in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter what's in yours statement. What we want to know is what the truth is. Were you dismissed for corruption and black marketeering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Were any such allegations made against you, whether they were true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of such stories being suggested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stories circulate about everybody, not just me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, again --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I proceed with another question which may perhaps help us little bit. Again, it is Exhibit Z578.1 which is in both English and Croatian for distribution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I address you in just a couple of words?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Let's see what this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, perhaps if the usher would be kind enough to put the document on the ELMO in Croatian, it would be helpful. This document dated 30th March signed by you -- you divest yourself, you remove yourself from running the treasury of the Kakanj HVO and you essentially turn over these duties to Mr. Franjo Maric, why? What is the reason that you are doing this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I was no longer in charge of the treasury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did that come to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It came -- it followed from my cessation of duty, of the duty at the Kakanj HVO, so anything that the HVO had in its possession, I turned over to the new official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And why did you cease to be president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps that is the same as why I may no longer be the representative in the parliament in the next election, because I may not get re-elected. So I ceased to be because the representatives who were legally elected decided that they no longer wanted me to lead them, but rather the man by the name of Blasko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that Pavlovic was elected and not appointed to cover your position? I'd just like that to be clear because the milinfosum suggests otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have different ways of elections. There are elections at legal, municipal and higher levels and there are elections within the parties and certain bodies, so within a body, members of the body may appoint an official.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then did you stay active in the HVO activities after Mr. Pavlovic became president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I just transferred into the military component of the HVO as the commander's assistant or advisor for political affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it easy to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that. Was it difficult to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not difficult at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So going from the civilian side to the military side was not a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could possibly just tell me, and we can do it either through -- I'll just ask, you were still active and working with Mr. Pavlovic on HVO matters, is that correct? After you left the position, were you still doing some civilian matters as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me just ask you something, at the time when you ceased to be President of the HVO, were there allegations at that time that you were involved in corruption and black marketeering. You told us earlier that you heard of such allegations being made. I'm asking whether at the time when you ceased to be president, when you were replaced by Mr. Franjo Maric, were those allegations being made against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, such stories, and I'm not talking about the specific allegations, such stories are still in circulation today. The investigation and the order of Mr. Blaskic was also mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [inaudible]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can ask for one further point for clarification before the break. Mr. Sljivic exactly, and I mean a date, exactly when did you stop being the president of the HVO Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if this is a convenient moment to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, as far as I am concerned, you can take it fairly shortly after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There are a couple of points I'd like to make about the relationships.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn now. Mr. Sljivic, during the adjournment, which will be for half an hour, don't speak to anyone, please, about your evidence and don't let anybody speak to you until it's over about it, and that does include members of the Defence team. Yes, we'll be back, please, half past 11.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, the initial summary which the Defence provided to the Prosecution indicated that heavy emphasis would be placed on your attesting to the absence of influence of Dario Kordic in the municipality of Kakanj. However, your testimony seems to be quite the opposite, and I wanted to ask, please, if you can describe your relationship, in a word, with Dario Kordic. Would you describe it as one of mentor, or were you a political admirer? Please help us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When it comes to my relationship with Mr. Kordic and his influence on the overall developments in the territory of the municipality of Kakanj, this is best attested to not by my statement but by the statement of Mr. Celebic, who was the mayor of the municipality of Kakanj, and at that time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I'm asking you about your relationship with Dario Kordic; not anybody else's, yours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1992, at the very beginning when all the roads for normal assault communication were blocked, then the population of the municipality of Kakanj had to face up to the problem as to how to survive the winter. During that period of time, for the citizens of the municipality of Kakanj, I managed to ensure, through the extraordinary help of Mr. Kordic and partly myself, where I could manage, to provide seed for the sowing season, fuel, whatever else was needed to feed the population, because at that time humanitarian organisations were not yet adequately represented in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so that every municipality had to fend for itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that Kordic assisted your municipality in getting humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in part humanitarian aid, through finished products and, in part, through seed stock for potatoes and other crops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said, "In 1992, at the very beginning," can you please pinpoint a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly, it could have been April or May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would the usher please distribute -- well, we can put it back up on the ELMO. It was previously admitted, Z87. I'm sorry, it was not. I thought it was. Z87. It is both in Croatian and in English. I apologise for no French translation at this time. May I ask for it also to be on the ELMO to assist -- possibly assist the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivic, you're looking at a decision issued under the hand of Dario Kordic on 3rd of May, 1992. This is the decision which appoints you as the head of the HVO in Kakanj. It's also to be noted it indicates that the Main Staff of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna has backed this appointment. Why you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was the lawfully-elected councilman in the municipal hall of Kakanj. Therefore, my legitimacy, the lawfulness of this, were confirmed by the lawful multi-party elections. And I presume that when people nominated me for this post, in addition to all other qualities that an individual might have, I suppose this was yet another quality, that I was both a legitimate and lawful representative of people in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mrs. Somers. I'd like to put this question to the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: the Croatian Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and apparently this decision appoints Mr. Pavo Sljivic to the position of president. I'd like to know whether he was appointed to the position of president of the HVO in Kakanj, so I'd like to ask the witness how he reads item 2 in this decision; Roman II, possibly. In other words, did Mr. Kordic have the authority, the necessary authority, to appoint him to the position of HVO president in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. I can't really see it well on the monitor, so could I look at the -- could I have the original to see what it says? Oh, I have it. I see, I see, it's here. Under item 2 of the decision, it says the president of the HVO of the municipality of Kakanj was designated by the president of the HVO, the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna. At that time, the president of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna was Mr. Mate Boban, and the vice-president, as far as I can remember, was Mr. Kordic, so that I see nothing questionable in this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it normal for this decision to be signed by Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: No, it is not common. I mean 99 per cent of all the cases, it must have been signed by Mr. Boban, and now I really cannot remember the circumstances and why this is so. If you asked me, "Who signed this decision," I would have answered you, "Mr. Boban."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my question is as follows: Does this mean that Mr. Kordic signed this decision in his capacity as HVO authority?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I cannot really affirm with certainty which office Mr. Kordic held at the time, but I am positive that whenever I asked for help to provide the people in the municipality of Kakanj with basic necessities, people usually instructed me -- in the absence of Mr. Boban and his associates, people sometimes told me to go to Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So given the rather special relationship that appears between you and Mr. Kordic, if he were to come to Kakanj, would you consider this an event of significance?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic came to Kakanj only for religious holidays, that is, for the patron saints of municipalities, for anniversaries. And on such occasions, I already mentioned in my statement that one of the occasions was the marking the celebration of St. Peter and St. Paul, the patron saints of the Kakanj province.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what patron saint had a special day on the 30th of September 1992? Let me ask you first, set the stage a little bit so I don't take you by surprise. There was a meeting, actually it was in Bobovac Kraljeva Sutjeska on the 30th of September 1992 involving essentially all of the Presidency of the Kakanj HVO. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exhibit number for this, which I would ask the Court to consider. It has been already admitted. It is Z229, but it is a very important document. This meeting, oddly, does not have your name in the roster of those present but if you say you were there, it would be logical.

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I have to see the document. It could be something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the meeting that is the subject of this document? At the end it is "Dopredsjednik HVO Pero Ruzic" who signed, but do you recall the meeting?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I chaired this meeting, but Dario Kordic did not attend this meeting, and Zvonko Duznovic did not attend it. Mr. Anto Pejcinovic was there. And the event that I said I attended was the mass celebrated at Stari Grad Bobovac where Bosnian kings had their seed, and that was in the May, I think, 1992. And I claim full responsibility that I chaired this meeting as the HVO president, and that neither Mr. Kordic nor Mr. Duznovic was present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I must confess then that it is surprise; that there is extensive dialogues between Dario Kordic or his alter ego and a number of members of the Kakanj municipality. Now, if you are saying that Mr. Kordic was not there, I'm afraid I'd probably have to challenge that or ask you to explain why this meeting is the subject -- represents so much angst on the various members of the municipality of Kakanj who are apparently unable to get direction to know whether to go with their Muslim cohabitants or to take a different path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just read the document. Can you refer him to some references.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. On your page in Croatian on page two, where it says, it says at the bottom, it has a Kordic quote. It will probably be in the English also page two. Yes, it would be, "I would like to greet you all but it would not be wise for me to give a speech at the start. I would like everybody to participate with at least two or three sentences and then I will make suggestions at the end."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, just read that passage and then the following passage in which Mr. Kordic is quoted as saying, "This meeting was agreed only yesterday in Vares." Just read through that. Now Mr. Sljivic, having read that, do you think, in fact, it may be possible that Mr. Kordic was at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I can affirm that such minutes, that the HVO in Kakanj never wrote such a long record of a meeting, such a long one, in so many pages, and with all these quotes. I claim to you, and I am under oath, that such a meeting with -- that one of such a meetings with these participants was chaired by me, and at the invitation only Mr. Anto Pejcinovic accepted the invitation, the HVO president in Vares. This is the first time I've seen this. You can ask me anything you like about this, but I cannot comment on it nor -- and I cannot say anything about the contents of this as this is the first time I see this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why do you think, then, that this document could be in the form that it is if Mr. Kordic was in fact not at the meeting at all?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I am sorry, I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why do you think that it is in the form which it is, that is, with extensive quotation from Mr. Kordic if he was not present, as you say, at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot answer that. I know that when I -- I was the president of the Croat Defence Council and without my knowledge, nobody could arrange such a meeting. And I see here that everybody's name is mentioned here but my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, then, that you were not -- that you were not at the meeting? There is a passage on page three in English and let me see if it's on -- where it would be -- which says essentially, "I, from Branko Pendic..."

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I have just received information that the president is in Zagreb and could not go to Germany." And then Mr. Kordic makes a response. Now, it's unclear which president is referred to. Is it possible, in your opinion, that you were not at this meeting, that you may have confused it with another meeting and Mr. Ruzic, your vice president, the deputy president, covered for you?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: At that time , I could not even get through to Zagreb because it was very difficult to do that. One had to take a helicopter and used all sorts of channels to get through, and I wasn't even thinking of going to Germany at the time, nor could I go and to get stuck in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I may suggest to you that perhaps your memory is failing you but -- or else everyone else's words were concocted. But on the assumption that this meeting did take place, and with the Chamber's permission, because I think it is important to raise these points, it is an admitted document. I would just like to ask if any of the content and just a few points, was discussed with you later or if you agree with some of the points that were raised at this meeting of a number of persons from Kakanj and Vares and which meeting suggests a great concern for the future of the municipality. Do you recall anyone ever telling you if you didn't hear it yourself that Kordic said, on page three of the document, "There is no more waiting for the Croatian people. We should withdraw our representatives from the legal municipal government and form our own." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: Regarding the concern of the Croatian population in Kakanj municipality, it existed at that time as it continues to exist to date. What I say is that I led one of these meetings and we discussed a very difficult situation of the Croatian population in Kakanj because of the large number of refugees from eastern Bosnia which we had in Kakanj and because of the encirclement that we were in. It wasn't only the Kakanj HVO that was concerned with that, but also the representatives of the Muslim population were concerned about this disruption of balance of the population so the concern was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But if you read the list of attendees, I see no Muslim names or representatives here, and the issue was not encirclement, the issue in this document is what is Kakanj supposed to do about it's future in the HZ HB, and that is the issue. How to survive, whether to revert to previous relationships with Muslims or to go forward. And I turn your attention, please look in English, it would be on page four. The gentleman's name Franjo Maric to whom you turned over the treasury duties in 1993, Mr. Maric is quoted in English on page four about -- he's making a reference to parity and the notion of parity is dealt with by Mr. Kordic right below. Let me quote, "The SDA," by Maric, "The SDA is prepared to divide the commercial property on the basis of parity, but there will be problems with the physical division." And Kordic says, "Parity will make us a part of the Muslim community. There is no more parity because they will take over in one or two years because in that way, you recognise the Muslim ethnic community. That is a political decision. They depend on us. They don't have to go through Vitez and Kiseljak to Croatia, but they shall not go through if they do not permit a Croatian municipality. That means they have to beg us, because they can't reach Ploce. They beg us, not the other way around, because you do not go to Europe through Pale." Excuse me, I'm being pointed out, it should read, "They have to go through Vitez," not, "they don't have to go through Vitez." Further down, Mr. Kordic also says, "It is a question of time," this is point number four under the Dario Kordic quote. "It is a question of time whether we will take or give up what is ours. It has been written down that Vares and Kakanj are in the HZ Herceg-Bosna. The Muslims are losing morale and then it will end with"give us what you will." All refugees want to go to Central Bosnia. Let them settle in the Muslim municipality." The last point on that page, Mr. Kordic says, "We have to destroy them economically." A comment. Are you familiar with any of the dialogue that is recorded on these pages? Was it brought to your attention if, in fact, you were not there? Was it brought to your attention as president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I remembered the part that talks about the parity, that is, the establishment of power in the Kakanj municipality. That was a maximum, perhaps even more, in terms of the conditions of the Croatian population in their negotiations with the Muslim side. As it is written here, this would mean a suicide for the Croatian people if anyone was to advocate this passage that was quoted. In this case, we did not need the HVO. It would be just signing off on a disaster for the Croatian population, and the Croatian government did not work against its own people. We were driven out not because we were trying to occupy 200.000 Muslims, the 16.000 of us in Kakanj, but the 200.000 Muslims wiped out all Croatian villages in the territory of Kakanj municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you, but not at the time of this meeting. What you are telling us was not the prevailing set of circumstances at the time of this meeting, was it, was it?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: You are trying to make me answer questions about events which did not exist, and I was not present there, so if I say that I don't know something, and if I wasn't there, and if I said I was at a similar meeting, you should respect that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with Mr. Kordic's assertion, which is found in English on page 2 of this document, where he says -- it says: "The situation in Kakanj is specific. Relationships are strained by the activities of the HVO OS, which developed from the idea of the Croatian people in Kakanj."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you slow down, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "There were also problems in the way the Croatian people were organised, and all this contributed to problems and weakness in the civil authorities because," and this is the part I would like to emphasise, "working in Kakanj is not like working in Busovaca. That is why the legal authorities functioned and they were Muslim. All this complicated relations. The people from Kakanj came and asked, 'What should we do?'" Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I couldn't find in time the page. It's page 4, as far as I could follow your quote. Was this page 2 or page 4, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In English, it was page 4. It is most likely page 3, but I'd like to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we're being helped by this. You can make your points in due course in comment --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I certainly will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- but the answers are not necessarily assisting us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I shall move on to another point. We will leave this document, and the points in it, of course, are points that it is the position of the Prosecution, of course, that this is a legitimate [transcript read in error "illegitimate"] meeting, Your Honour, and we'll proceed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that -- you called yourself a refugee from Kakanj. Can I ask you this, before I ask you a little bit more about your definition of "refugee": Which constitutive or constituent nation did you view as the enemy, as it were, requiring defence in 1992 and up until mid-1993? I'm sorry. Pardon me for interrupting you, Mr. Sljivic, but the transcript reads "this is an illegitimate meeting". It should read "legitimate meeting". I beg your pardon. Did you follow my question? If not, I shall repeat it.

utterances.speaker: Here we have in front of us a decision from
utterances.text: I followed the question. Your Honour, just a correction, Your Honours. There are two categories, Your Honours. There is a displaced person and there is a refugee. I am a displaced person because I stayed within Bosnia and Herzegovina. Refugees are those who have left the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as far as the constituent population against whom we needed to defend ourselves in early 1992, it was clear that the Croatian Defence Council and ABiH both defended themselves against the so-called Yugoslav People's Army, which in my judgement carried out an aggression against the integral State of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting it is the Serb segment of the JNA? In other words, if I had to ask you for whether it was Serb, Croat, or Muslim, you would select the term "Serb" as the enemy?
